newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX hit by Hoechst, weaker dollar ends down.
newsitem.headline: German DAX hit by Hoechst, weaker dollar ends down.

text.p: German shares ended sharply lower on Wednesday, with Hoechst AG to blame for much of the fall after a surprise move to drop plans for a separate listing of its pharmaceuticals unit.
The IBIS DAX index, which measures electronic trade in 30 German blue-chip stocks, ended down 48.55 points at 3,382.40 points, or a loss of 1.42 percent.

The DAX index earlier ended bourse trade down 45.19 points, or a loss of 1.31 percent, at 3,415.40 as the index was also hit by the sluggish dollar, which was trading under 1.71 marks, and Wall Street's mixed overnight results.
Shares in Hoechst tumbled as much as 13 percent in active bourse dealings after saying it would not list its Hoechst Marion Roussel (HMR) unit on the stock market.
Dealers said the market was surprised and disappointed by the decision, saying such a move had been widely been expected as a means of increasing shareholder value.
"The announcement today has taken all speculative interest out of the stock," said one London-based trader.
The trader added that he expected a number of downgrade recommendations on Hoechst in the coming days follow the company's meeting with analysts on Wednesday.

Hoechst on Tuesday had already disappointed investors by reporting a 2.5 percent drop in sales to 50.9 billion marks and saying it pre-tax profit climbed by 29.06 percent to 5.28 billion marks, largely due to earnings from divestments.
Hoechst ended the day down 6.06 marks, or down 8.06 percent, at 69.14 marks.
Elsewhere, dealers complained of a lack of fresh news to drive the market upwards. "Trading volumes outside Hoechst are small at the moment, which is a bit worrying," said one dealer.
But Deutsche Telekom continued its rise of recent days as investors sought out stocks that have not fully participated in the DAX's recent rally.
Germany's monopoly telecom group ended up 56 pfennigs at 35.39 marks after briefly hitting a new high of 35.95 in bourse dealings.
